title: Comparison of principal local tests with the canonical small-site ideal tests
statement: For a ringed site (C,J,R) with independent site universes and coefficient universe containing them, let t be a global section and P any object of its unbounded module derived category. Use locallyComplete of [def-sf-regular-roos-koszul-data], which tests every slice section that is in the image of multiplication by t. Restrict R and t to the canonical small model [def-sf-koszul-small-model-completed-tensor], obtaining S and a, and use independent derived localization universes. Then locallyComplete(R,t,P) is equivalent to IsLocallyDerivedRingedIdealComplete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete] for the unit module of S mapping to itself by multiplication by a, evaluated at the derived-equivalence image of P. This is only an equivalence of local predicates; it does not construct or assert a completion reflector. The predicate is defined even without assuming the multiplication map monic.

source.place: Tags 0999, 099B and 0A0E; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA and 03DG. The comparison step of lem-sf-principal-strict-limit-reflector.

proof.text: Use the induced equivalence on every slice and the exact slice restriction square. The section localization universal property followed by the sheafification comparison identifies the localizations at corresponding sections. The derived-Hom restriction comparison computes the same test through the exact slice equivalence, using independent derived localization universes.

A slice section is determined by its terminal value, by naturality for the unique map to the identity arrow. After identifying corresponding sections, the exact-multiple equation is the image-of-multiplication equation in the small-site predicate. The ordinary and universe-generalized localizations and derived Hom lifts agree by their construction and localization universal property.

Exact slice equivalences preserve and reflect zero objects. Every original object is isomorphic to the inverse-equivalence image of a small-model object, and the induced equivalences of slices identify these tests under that isomorphism. Apply the preceding zero-object equivalence in both directions for all slice sections. No regularity, K-flatness or product exactness is used.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0999, 099B and 0A0E, with the size and normalization comparisons expanded for the existing Lean interfaces.

lean.statement:
theorem principal_strict_small_model_local_tests
    (t : (SheafOfModules.unit (ring.{c, v, r} R)).sections)
    (P : DerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{c, v, r} R)) :
    locallyComplete.{c, v, r, w} R t P ↔
      IsLocallyDerivedRingedIdealComplete (KoszulSmallModel.ring.{c, v, max c v r} R)
        (SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose _
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj
            (KoszulSmallModel.ring.{c, v, max c v r} R)))
        (ringedKoszulScalar (KoszulSmallModel.ring.{c, v, max c v r} R)
          (KoszulSmallModel.globalSection.{c, v, max c v r} R ⟨t.val, t.property⟩))
        ((KoszulSmallModel.derivedEquiv.{c, v, max c v r, w, w₀} R).functor.obj P)
